issues.note: 64971fab · resumable-upload.ts (tus-js-client) + app/api/uploads/session-token; 9/9 + 4/4 — ≥ 8 MB uses the resumable path; smaller files, and any file whose resumable attempt fails for any reason, fall back to the original single-PUT unchanged. issues.title: Live-model golden suite
issues.note: f2339894 - live_golden.py + CLI + pytest suite; 64 tests (2 skipped by design), tests/golden/ 279 total, 0 failures — Before this, all 12 golden files were offline - they proved the plumbing and nothing about what the model produces; the README carried a section titled *“Live golden run … TODO”*. The design problem was the SKIP, not the suite: a live suite that silently passes with no credential is worse than none, because it reads as evidence. Four layers: the resolver sees through the test-gemini-key placeholder (asserted in this repo own test env); a second gate (CROWMARK_LIVE_GOLDEN=1) means holding a key can never cause a dial-out; the skip reason names the variable and ends *“NOT RUN - this is not a pass”*; and summarise() forces passed: 0 on a skipped run. A live-call failure is not a quality regression: status is three-way, the classifier reads the chained message, and exit code 3 exists because neither 0 nor 1 can honestly say “the model was unreachable”. Assertions are properties, never exact strings, so it cannot be muted by rewording; the banned-construction list comes from the shipped system prompt; and gate_verdict_consistent re-runs the gate independently rather than trusting the pipeline own verdict. All 8 proved to fail, including against a forged {"passed": true}.

issues.title: Engagement analytics on delivered proposals
issues.note: d413e8fe + 1015eeb4 - migration 20261520000000 applied staging+prod, verified by object; 35 tests, mutation-tested — ⚠ The row premise is partly wrong and could not be built as written. There is no “delivered proposal” to instrument: nothing is submitted through this platform (crowmark_esubmission returns 501, every connector returns "packaged"), so proposals leave as downloads and are pasted into the buyer portal - once a file leaves, nothing is observable and no schema change fixes that. The CrowMark report “share” link is also internal, not a buyer channel. Built for the two genuine buyer-facing surfaces instead. Found on the way: recordReportAccess is write-only - four writers, zero readers. The load-bearing privacy decision is a column type: occurred_on is a DATE, not a TIMESTAMPTZ, because a share token often goes to exactly one named evaluator, so a precise timestamp would let the issuing org reconstruct *“opened at 23:40”* by linkage alone with no identifier stored. Verified on prod: zero columns matching email/IP/user-agent/referrer/visitor-id/session-id. Never-opened returns open_count: null, never 0, and three states stay distinct - not_opened_yet vs not_published (reporting an off link as unopened blames the buyer for the org own setting) vs count_only. A lookup failure returns 503, never an empty payload - rendering an outage as “the buyer never opened your proposal” is the worst bug this endpoint could have. Retention 24 months, now scheduled (1015eeb4) - it was documented and implemented but nothing called it, and here the window is part of the privacy case for recording opens at all.
